title: Southern Fried-Style Coleslaw
subtitle: Creamy, sweet and tangy coleslaw just like the fast food version
excerpt: A soft, sweet-tangy coleslaw with finely shredded white cabbage and carrot dressed in a generous mayonnaise-cider-vinegar dressing. This is the mild, dairy-creamy style served alongside fried chicken across southern-fried restaurants.
sourceNotes: The creamy American diner coleslaw has roots in Dutch and German koolsla (cabbage salad). The sweet-tangy mayonnaise version became standard in American fast-food chains from the 1950s. The basic formula (cabbage, carrot, mayo, vinegar, sugar) is documented in mid-20th-century American cookbooks including those from Church Ladies Recipe collections and American diner archives.

recipe.batchNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead. The coleslaw softens as it sits, which is the desired texture for this style.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dress at least an hour before serving to let the cabbage soften and absorb the dressing.

content.text: Southern fried-style coleslaw is the soft, milky-sweet version: finely shredded cabbage and carrot in a generous mayo-based dressing with enough vinegar and sugar to stay interesting. It is deliberately mild and creamy, designed to cool down spiced fried food. The ratio of dressing to cabbage is higher than in a traditional slaw.
Shred the cabbage as finely as possible. The finer the shred, the softer and more cohesive the finished coleslaw. A mandoline makes quick work of it; a sharp knife and patience work just as well.
Combine the shredded cabbage and grated carrot in a large bowl. Toss to mix.

Whisk together {{mayonnaise}} of mayonnaise, {{cider-vinegar}} of cider vinegar, {{caster-sugar}} of sugar, {{english-mustard}} of English mustard, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Taste: it should be sweet, tangy and well seasoned. Pour over the cabbage and toss to coat thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Toss again before serving.

items.cause: Cabbage releases water as it sits, diluting the dressing.
items.fix: For a drier result, salt the shredded cabbage and leave for 20 minutes, then squeeze out excess liquid before dressing.

items.cause: Too much vinegar for the amount of sugar.
items.fix: Add an extra teaspoon of sugar and a splash more mayonnaise to balance. Taste and adjust.

items.cause: Not enough resting time in the dressing.
items.fix: Leave for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight. The acidity of the vinegar softens the shreds over time.

content.text: This coleslaw exists to sit next to fried chicken and cut through the richness. The high ratio of dressing to cabbage, the sweetness, the yield to the fork: all of these are design features rather than accidents. It is a deliberate softening of the sharper European slaw tradition, made for a context where the main event is spiced and crisp.
